prompt: Which of the following are advantages of financial indicators?

options.text: They provide a very concise measure of performance.
When based on accounting figures, they are relatively reliable.
They can easily be aggregated and/or compared.
They are inexpensive and simple to compute.
They are good predictors of future performance.

explanation: Conciseness, reliability, aggregability/comparability and low cost are advantages. Predicting the future is precisely one of their weaknesses.

prompt: Which of the following are limitations of measurement systems that include only financial indicators?

options.text: They may give a very partial or even inappropriate view of performance.
They do not explain the causes of discrepancies and give little guidance on corrective actions.
They risk focusing managers on short-term results at the expense of medium/long-term performance.
They are poor at predicting future performance.
They are expensive and complicated to compute.

explanation: The four limitations: partial view, no insight into causes, short-termism, poor predictive power. Cost is actually an advantage (they are inexpensive).

prompt: A division's ROCE drops by three points and its manager only receives financial indicators. Which statements apply?

options.text: The indicator signals the problem but does not reveal its causes.
The financial indicator alone gives little guidance on the corrective action needed.
The drop reflects the financial consequences of actions already taken rather than predicting future performance.
Because the indicator is concise, it tells the manager exactly which operational lever to pull.

explanation: Conciseness is both an advantage and a limit: financial indicators summarise but don't explain. They are lagging measures of consequences.

prompt: Why are financial indicators poor at predicting future performance?

options.text: They measure the financial consequences of actions that have already been taken.
They are based on unreliable data.
They do not capture the operational levers that drive future results.
They cannot be aggregated.

explanation: Financial indicators are backward-looking (consequences of past actions). They are relatively reliable and easy to aggregate.

statement: Financial indicators are poor at predicting future performance because they measure the financial consequences of actions already taken.
explanation: They are backward-looking.

statement: Financial indicators are costly and complex to compute.
explanation: They are inexpensive and simple to compute – one of their advantages.

statement: Measurement systems with only financial indicators can focus managers' attention on short-term results to the detriment of medium- and long-term performance.
explanation: Short-termism is a key limitation.

statement: Because they are concise, financial indicators provide a detailed understanding of the causes of performance gaps.
explanation: Conciseness means they do NOT explain the causes of discrepancies.

statement: When based on accounting figures, financial indicators are relatively reliable.
explanation: Reliability is one of their advantages.

prompt: State the main advantages and the main limitations of financial indicators for management control.
modelAnswer: Advantages: very concise measure of performance; relatively reliable when based on accounting figures; easy to aggregate and compare; inexpensive and simple to compute. Limitations of purely financial measurement systems: partial or even inappropriate view of performance; no understanding of the causes of discrepancies, hence little guidance on corrective actions; risk of short-termism; poor at predicting future performance.
keyPoints: Advantages: easy to aggregate / compare, inexpensive & simple
Limitation: partial / inappropriate view of performance
Limitation: no causes → little guidance on corrective action
Limitation: short-termism and poor prediction of future performance

prompt: To meet this year's profit target, a division manager cuts maintenance, training and R&D spending. Which limitation of financial-only measurement systems does this illustrate?

options.text: The risk of focusing managers' attention on short-term results to the detriment of medium- and long-term performance
The high cost of computing financial indicators
The difficulty of aggregating financial indicators

explanation: Financial indicators can push managers towards short-term results at the expense of medium- and long-term performance.

prompt: For a hospital or a non-profit organisation, measuring performance only with financial indicators …

options.text: may give a very partial view of performance
may even give an inappropriate view of performance
captures all relevant performance dimensions
is impossible, because financial indicators cannot be computed there

explanation: By definition financial indicators measure financial aspects only, which can be very partial or even inappropriate in some organisations.

prompt: The conciseness of financial indicators is …

options.text: an advantage: they provide a very concise measure of performance
a limitation: they do not reveal the causes of discrepancies
irrelevant for management control

explanation: Conciseness is double-edged: concise summary of performance, but little understanding of causes and corrective actions.

prompt: Which advantages of financial indicators relate to the qualities expected of measurements (validity, reliability, ease of implementation)?

options.text: Relative reliability when based on accounting figures
Ease of implementation: inexpensive and simple to compute
Perfect validity for every performance objective

explanation: Financial indicators score well on reliability and ease of implementation, but their validity can be limited because they only capture financial aspects.

prompt: A group wants to compare and consolidate the performance of its 12 divisions in a single figure. Which advantage of financial indicators is useful here?

options.text: They can easily be aggregated and/or compared.
They predict future performance well.
They explain the causes of discrepancies.

explanation: Financial indicators are easy to aggregate and compare across units.

statement: Financial indicators measure performance on financial aspects alone.
explanation: That is why, by definition, they may give a partial or even inappropriate view of performance in some organisations.

statement: Financial indicators provide strong guidance on which corrective actions are needed when goals are not achieved.
explanation: Being concise, they do not explain the causes of discrepancies and therefore give little guidance on corrective actions.

statement: Financial indicators can easily be aggregated and compared.
explanation: This is one of their key advantages.

statement: Because of their limitations, financial indicators are of little use for measuring company performance.
explanation: Their many advantages make them essential measures of performance; the limits concern measurement systems that include only financial indicators.

statement: Financial indicators are leading indicators of future performance.
explanation: They measure the financial consequences of actions already taken and are poor at predicting future performance.

statement: Measurement systems that include only financial indicators have limitations even though financial indicators themselves have many advantages.
explanation: Advantages: concise, relatively reliable, easy to aggregate/compare, cheap. Limits appear when they are used alone.

prompt: Explain why measurement systems based only on financial indicators may lead to short-termism.
modelAnswer: Financial indicators measure the financial consequences of actions already taken, typically over short periods. If managers are steered and evaluated only on them, they may favour actions that improve short-term results (e.g. cutting R&D, training or maintenance) to the detriment of medium- and long-term performance, which financial indicators are poor at anticipating.
keyPoints: Financial indicators measure past/short-term financial consequences
Managers' attention focused on short-term results
Detriment of medium- and long-term performance

prompt: Explain why financial indicators give little guidance for corrective action when goals are not achieved.
modelAnswer: Financial indicators measure performance in a very concise way: they signal that a gap exists but do not provide an understanding of the causes of the discrepancy. Without knowing the operational drivers behind the gap, managers get little guidance on the corrective actions needed.
keyPoints: Signal the gap but not its causes
Hence little guidance on corrective actions
